name: State Farm Olathe

model_completeness.definition: All eight contribution-account categories contain sourced or labeled modeled values, and GDP, employment, and wage county-comparison modules are populated. Comparison gaps are descriptive and do not establish causal facility effects.

research_value: SEC property evidence links capital asset, lease, and later occupancy; lease date is not commissioning.

history.date_note: This is a stored historical observation. Completion, grand opening, lease and operating-by dates are not automatically commissioning dates. Campus timing does not date every building.

sources.title: IM3 Open Source Data Center Atlas, release 2026.02.09

research_updates.title: County parcel links HMC ownership and the State Farm data center
research_updates.notes: Johnson County identifies HMC Data Center 2 LLC as parcel owner at 24400 W Valley Parkway and labels the commercial building STATE FARM MUTUAL AUTOMOBILE INSURANCE CO, Computer data center. The parcel account supports the value, bill and payment series. Paid totals cover multiple taxing entities and are not treated as city-only or county-only receipts.

source.title: Johnson County Property Tax Office — State Farm data-center parcel R662349
source.publisher: Johnson County, Kansas Property Tax Office
source.notes: The official parcel page identifies owner HMC Data Center 2 LLC, situs 24400 W Valley Parkway, quick reference R662349 and real-estate tax ID DP69210000 0001. Its commercial-building section names STATE FARM MUTUAL AUTOMOBILE INSURANCE CO and classifies the structure as a computer data center. Value History reports 2021–2025 appraised and assessed totals. Bills report 2019–2025 total taxes due, equal amounts paid and zero balances; the 2025 installments show payment dates December 4, 2025 and May 19, 2026. Tax totals cover all listed taxing entities and are not allocated here to city, county, schools or other recipients.

research_updates.title: Project boundary, ownership and operating chronology audit
research_updates.notes: SEC filings from 2017 and 2025, Johnson County parcel records, City planning materials and FCC records were reconciled by 24400 West Valley Parkway, the State Farm Data Center name, SFDC Cedar Creek, quick reference R662349 and tax ID DP69210000 0001. They establish a single approximately 20-acre property built in 2016, State Farm possession by early 2017, later HMC Data Center 2 LLC parcel ownership and continuing State Farm tenancy. Financing borrowers, parcel owners and operator are not conflated, and no neighboring U.S. Bank facility or wider two-property State Farm portfolio amount is assigned here.

source.title: Citigroup Commercial Mortgage Trust 2017-C4 Free Writing Prospectus
source.notes: The filed term sheet identifies a 193,953-square-foot data center on 20.1 acres in Olathe, constructed in 2016 as a State Farm build-to-suit. It reports 60,515 square feet of raised floor, 6,660 kW critical IT load, 100% State Farm occupancy, lease commencement in November 2016 and tenant possession and use. Loan, purchase-price, rent and appraisal figures are financing or valuation measures and are not normalized as local economic contributions.

research_updates.title: Construction and permit-value audit
research_updates.notes: City annual permit reports, planning files and indexed permit histories were searched for 2015-2026 by BC15-0148, BC17-0041, SFDC Cedar Creek, State Farm, Kansas City Data Center and the exact address. Official reports support separate $81,555,000 new-construction and $28,000,000 tenant-finish permit values. These administrative values are neither verified expenditures nor safely additive to each other or the SEC's $169,778,850 estimated cumulative capital figure; no worker hours, construction payroll, schedule, equipment split or realized construction job count was found.

source.title: City of Olathe 2015 Year in Review — fourth-quarter nonresidential permits
source.notes: The official planning report lists permit BC15-0148, STATE FARM-NEW CONST, at 24400 W Valley Parkway in SFDC Cedar Creek. It reports 198,000 square feet and an $81,555,000 cost for privately owned new construction. The permit cost is an administrative amount rather than audited expenditure, local procurement, payroll or total capital investment.

research_updates.title: Supplier and procurement audit — participants found, payments absent
research_updates.notes: Official permit reports and indexed contractor, architect and engineer materials were searched for State Farm Olathe, Kansas City Data Center, Corgan, GBA Builders, U.S. Engineering, supplier, vendor, contract and payment. A secondary permit index associates Corgan with foundation work, but its value is excluded because primary provenance and overlap are unresolved. No contract amount, paid supplier total, vendor address at payment time or Johnson County local-retention share was found, and no permit value is allocated among suppliers.

source.title: Corgan Associates permit history
source.notes: The commercial permit index associates Corgan Associates with a foundation permit for Kansas City Data Center at the exact address. Because this is a secondary index and its displayed valuation may overlap or conflict with the official City new-construction amount, no value is normalized. Searches for Corgan, GBA Builders, U.S. Engineering and other project participants did not yield primary paid amounts, supplier locations at payment time or Johnson County retained shares.

research_updates.title: Parcel, fiscal-revenue and public-cost audit
research_updates.notes: Johnson County assessor and treasurer records were rechecked for R662349 and DP69210000 0001, including 2021-2025 values and 2019-2025 bills, paid amounts and balances. Olathe ACFRs, budgets, agendas and financing materials were searched for State Farm, JDM III, HMC Data Center 2, the address and project-specific service or infrastructure cost. Parcel taxes span several recipients; no recipient allocation, marginal police, fire, road, utility, administrative or debt cost, reimbursement total or same-scope net fiscal position was found.

research_updates.title: State and local incentive audit — no project award amount located
research_updates.notes: Kansas Commerce transparency, PEAK and HPIP materials, Kansas Revenue tax-expenditure reports, City financial and agenda records and indexed bond records were searched by State Farm, Kansas City Data Center, JDM III SF Kansas City DC, HMC Data Center 2 and the exact address. No project-specific executed award, certified job or investment commitment, claimed tax benefit, local abatement schedule, bond subsidy or counterfactual tax amount was located. General program rules and later data-center legislation are not treated as evidence that this 2015-2017 project received a benefit.

source.title: Kansas Department of Commerce Transparency Explorer
source.notes: The state transparency and program materials were searched for State Farm, Kansas City Data Center, JDM III SF Kansas City DC, HMC Data Center 2, the Olathe address, PEAK and HPIP. No award, executed agreement, certified benefit or claimed amount attributable to this property was found. Program eligibility is not evidence of receipt, and newer data-center incentives are not back-cast to the 2015-2017 work.

research_updates.title: Electricity, utility and resource-consumption audit
research_updates.notes: KCC current and archived dockets, City utility pages, SEC facility descriptions, operator environmental reports and indexed utility materials were searched for 2015-2026 by operator, address, owner entities, service agreement, tariff, load, electricity, water, wastewater, PUE and renewable terms. SEC filings support only 6.66 MW and 7.5 MW critical-IT-load capacity snapshots. No utility identity supported by a primary site record, special contract, observed demand, annual kWh, power bill, measured PUE, metered water, wastewater volume, rate class or account payment was found; capacity is not converted to consumption.

source.title: Kansas Corporation Commission docket filings search
source.notes: Current and archived docket indexes were searched for 2015-2026 using State Farm, 24400 West Valley Parkway, Kansas City Data Center, JDM III, HMC Data Center 2, data center and utility terms. No address-matched tariff, special contract, service agreement, observed load, bill, grid-upgrade cost or public subsidy was found.

research_updates.title: Environmental, generator and emergency-response audit
research_updates.notes: FCC, regional emergency-planning, EPA ECHO, Kansas environmental and indexed air, fuel, generator and discharge records were searched using the facility name and exact address. The FCC grant documents communications equipment and the regional plan identifies the site, but neither supplies generator count, fuel storage, run hours, emissions, discharge, resource consumption, incident history or attributable emergency-response cost. A 2016 Phase I statement in the SEC filing is environmental due diligence, not operating-performance evidence.

source.title: Regional Hazardous Materials Emergency Preparedness Plan
source.notes: The regional emergency-planning material identifies the State Farm Insurance Data Center at 24400 W Valley Parkway. It does not report site generator count, fuel storage, discharge, emissions, annual energy or water use, incident cost or project-attributable emergency-response expense. EPA ECHO and Kansas environmental searches likewise produced no quantitative address-matched operating record suitable for this account.

research_updates.title: Operations and workforce audit — facility capacity found, labor totals absent
research_updates.notes: SEC filings, State Farm careers and impact materials, City economic-development records and indexed job postings were searched for 2015-2026 by Olathe, exact address, data center, employee, contractor, technician, wage, payroll and residency. The filings establish area, tenant occupancy, operating chronology and critical IT load. No realized State Farm or contractor FTE, annual payroll, wage distribution, worker residence, operating purchase or facility revenue was public; a third-party technician vacancy is neither realized headcount nor a representative facility wage.

source.title: State Farm careers
source.publisher: State Farm Mutual Automobile Insurance Company
source.notes: Operator careers and indexed job results were searched by Olathe, exact address, data center, technician and facilities terms. No official realized facility headcount, employee-versus-contractor split, wage, payroll, residency or hiring series was found. A third-party technician vacancy is not treated as realized State Farm employment or representative compensation.

research_updates.title: Community and nonprofit-recipient audit — no facility transfer found
research_updates.notes: State Farm community-grant, impact, volunteer and press materials and indexed Olathe, Johnson County, school, nonprofit, first-responder, donation and grant results were searched for facility attribution, recipient, date and amount. No cash grant, in-kind value or volunteer-hour total tied to the Olathe data center was found. Company-wide giving, activity by local insurance agents and similarly named out-of-state State Farm data-center projects are excluded.

source.title: State Farm community grants program
source.publisher: State Farm Mutual Automobile Insurance Company
source.notes: The operator's program page and indexed local grant and volunteer results were searched for Olathe, Johnson County, the facility address and data-center attribution. No recipient, date and amount tied to this facility was located; activity by local agents or company-wide programs is not assigned to the data center.

research_updates.title: Planning, expansion and strategic-infrastructure audit
research_updates.notes: City planning, zoning, annual development reports, Legistar packets, transportation and infrastructure references were searched by address, SFDC Cedar Creek and operator or owner names. The public record supports the original building and later tenant finish and confirms that the area already includes another data center. No separately bounded State Farm expansion, publicly funded road or utility improvement, quantified strategic benefit, fiber subsidy or State Farm-specific infrastructure reimbursement was located.

source.title: Olathe planning packet G23-3676 / RZ23-0001
source.notes: The packet for adjacent development identifies existing State Farm and U.S. Bank data centers in the area and describes the established large-lot campus-office context. It supplies no State Farm-specific expansion value, employment, utility demand, public reimbursement or public-service cost.

research_updates.title: County outcomes and modeling-eligibility audit
research_updates.notes: The repository's 2001-2024 Johnson County BEA and BLS GDP, employment and wage series were reviewed alongside project chronology and nearby data-center context. No project-specific treatment exposure series, first-county-entry evidence, uncontaminated comparison set, pretrend diagnostic, placebo or robustness result supports a State Farm-attributable county effect. Missing construction labor, operations labor, suppliers, community transfers, actual resource use, incentives and public costs also lack cited site-allocation parameters, so no multiplier, utility, net-fiscal, break-even or causal model is added merely to complete categories.

source.title: Johnson County economic panel source and design audit
source.publisher: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis and U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics
source.notes: The repository county panel contains official annual Johnson County real GDP, employment and average-weekly-wage series for 2001-2024. The audit found no registered treatment timing, exposure isolation, uncontaminated control design, pretrend evidence, placebo test or robustness result sufficient to interpret a comparison as a State Farm facility effect; nearby pre-existing data-center activity also prevents an unsupported first-entry assumption.

economic_scope_note: Reviewed evidence batches at campus or company/county scope. No record is allocated to an individual inventory building. Source checking establishes what a document reports, not an independent audit or causal attribution. Monetary figures are nominal. Peak workforce is distinct from annual employment; source-year labels do not establish fiscal-year boundaries. Original forecasts remain forecasts until realization is verified. No cross-record benefit total is defined. Cumulative project costs are not annual expenditure. Tax receipts and incentive payments remain separate, with inferred taxpayer links disclosed. Contextual research updates do not count as economic amounts. Account tax bills are distinct from cash receipts and incentive-program fees. Tax years, calendar years and fiscal years retain their source basis; separate taxpayer accounts are not consolidated. Municipal developer rebates and taxpayer valuations have distinct subjects. Estimated actual property value and tax capacity are not tax receipts; payable-year valuations retain their earlier assessment date. Taxpayer values expressed in millions retain approximate precision and account-level separation. A current-year table can use an older valuation date and is not converted into an annual series. Facility real-property and business-personal-property accounts remain separate, and address-label discrepancies are disclosed. Michigan Industrial Facilities Tax accounts remain distinct from the underlying real parcel and from post-expiration personal-property accounts; annual account totals are not recipient-level government receipts. Permit construction values are administrative project amounts, not verified expenditure, and separate permits are not combined without proof that their scopes do not overlap. Repeated maintenance-year assessments are annual parcel stocks, not new investment flows. Mixed-use parcel assessments and taxable values are retained at whole-parcel scope and are not allocated to a data-center tenant or function by floor area. Operator-reported jobs supported remain distinct from direct employees and FTEs. Approved infrastructure grants are documented public commitments rather than verified disbursements or total public costs. Cumulative community funding remains separate from tax receipts, payroll and modeled multiplier effects. Reported facility power capacity is not measured electricity consumption or peak demand. Permit-listed emergency generators are not runtime, fuel-use or actual-emissions observations. A city largest-taxpayer table's personal-property assessment remains separate from the leasehold real-property account, tax bills, receipts and capital expenditure. TIF loan principal is financing rather than a grant or general-fund receipt; project-generated tax revenue pledged to repayment is retained as a separate public-financing flow and is not added to gross parcel distributions. Water-withdrawal and consumptive permit capacities are regulatory limits rather than measured use. Development-agreement local-labor preferences are requirements rather than realized participation, and operating employee snapshots remain distinct from customers' on-site staff and jobs forecasts. Audited City bond statements distinguish issuance draws, year-end principal, annual principal retired, interest and fees, pledged TIF revenue, debt-service-fund transfers and future principal-plus-interest commitments. These measures are not summed into a benefit or subsidy total. City pledged revenue, City debt-service-fund transfers and the private fund's project TIF revenue applied to loan repayment retain their separate source definitions because only the 2022 transfer and private-fund amount agree exactly. Developer testimony in public meeting minutes is retained as a source-attributed cumulative lower bound; local-contractor spending is not converted into payroll, worker counts, household spending or multiplier effects. Economic-improvement-district cost estimates and maximum owner assessments remain source projections until bond issuance, an assessment schedule, collections and expenditures are verified. A statutory financing cap is not a tax receipt, public expenditure or subsidy. Audited private equipment-financing balances are debt stocks rather than construction spending, public support or community benefit. Reported floor area and occupied-share values describe operating scale and utilization, not employment, revenue, power use or economic output. Contractor and engineer case studies document supplier roles and completion timing but do not establish payment amounts, worker residence, payroll or multiplier effects. State incentive contract amounts, expected jobs and paid-or-certified-to-date fields remain distinct; a zero paid/certified balance at an earlier reporting cutoff does not imply no later claims. Public charging-infrastructure awards are commitments rather than verified disbursements, private project investment or operating benefits. Qualitative payment descriptions without a defensible numeric bound remain research context rather than quantitative records. Program-reported actual qualified investment, certified tax-exemption value and certified tax-credit value remain separate cumulative measures; none is converted into annual spending, a cash grant, local revenue or causal impact. County Business Patterns observations are county-industry context, not project contributions: establishment counts are employer locations rather than data-center facilities, March employment is not an annual average, annual payroll spans the full NAICS cell, and disclosure noise, classification changes and geographic assignment limit comparisons. No CBP change is attributed to a study project. modeled_scope_note: Modeled contribution accounts for Apple Mesa / Maricopa County, Switch Citadel / Storey County, and Digital Crossroad Hammond / Lake County. Every required account category and county-comparison module contains sourced evidence or a visibly labeled modeled value. Public support is not netted against unmatched local revenues, unavailable public-service cost is represented by a break-even threshold rather than an invented net margin, county comparisons are descriptive rather than causal, and low-confidence transferred benchmarks remain explicit. Project fragments: prj_study_im3_building_00364289074: Corrective residual modeled account for Microsoft San Antonio. Eight transferred construction, labor, procurement, operating, and household-output scenarios were removed because their arbitrary capital shares, forecast-realization cases, local-purchase assumptions, and Virginia coefficients were not bounded by project observations. Only three low-confidence descriptive county comparisons remain: each uses the project's documented operating-by 2013 anchor and official Bexar County outcome data, has a finite fit-sensitivity envelope, and explicitly makes no causal attribution. The account intentionally remains incomplete because no defensible direct observation or residual model closes the supplier category. prj_study_im3_building_00377585075: Corrective DET01 synthesis. Only exact same-period tax-account arithmetic, its explicitly conditional public-cost break-even identity and a unit conversion of displayed municipal meter history remain. Construction, employment, supplier, household, electricity, cooling, emissions, wastewater and county-effect models were removed because the audit did not bound the missing project inputs. This account is intentionally incomplete where direct evidence remains unbounded. prj_study_im3_building_00460089167: Corrective audit retains six bounded residual calculations only: FY2025 county tax retained after the provisionally linked incentive, the identical marginal-service-cost break-even threshold, conversion of Meta-reported 2024 water withdrawal with source rounding, and three noncausal county comparison gaps with fit sensitivity. Ten models based on arbitrary capital timing, cost shares, FTE ratios, transferred operating/construction multipliers, fleet PUE, or wastewater ratios are removed. Supplier/local-procurement evidence remains unavailable, so the project is intentionally incomplete rather than backfilled. prj_study_im3_building_00464097467: Second-pass modeled contribution account after an expanded public-evidence audit. Direct county permits now cover historical construction values, assessor rolls cover a main-campus parcel stock, a county action covers water-right capacity, Apple reports 2025 campus electricity use, and recipient reports bound two community gifts. Those observations supersede the need for a modeled community proxy but do not supply Apple contractor job-years, construction payroll, annual operating payroll, supplier payments, taxes received, or public-service cost. The construction base therefore retains only the packet's explicit $163 million construction forecast and excludes equipment and historical capital; wide 0.5-1.5 transfer sensitivities expose the mismatch in the last-resort direct construction coefficients. The unsupported local-purchase-share and Virginia induced-output models are removed. No net-fiscal value or public-service-cost break-even is published. County outcome gaps remain descriptive benchmark applications with fit-sensitivity intervals and no causal-design metadata. prj_study_im3_building_00664938835: Second-pass Expedient Milwaukee / Franklin syntheses retained only after a documented 2007-2026 public-source audit. The account keeps a clearly labeled 2022 ownership-transfer anchor, a PB25-0303-only construction allocation sensitivity, an exact tax-equal public-cost break-even threshold, a capacity-based electricity engineering sensitivity, and three descriptive county comparison gaps. It removes transferred construction job-years, assumed local-purchase shares, supplier and household output extrapolations, and a duplicate modeled tax row because public sources did not establish realized site employment, supplier geography, household capture, or a need to restate the direct tax observations. PM25-0174 remains excluded for possible overlap. No synthesis is an observed result or fiscal net. prj_study_im3_building_00888253616: Residual synthesis after the SV1 public-source audit. It retains one exact tax-equal public-cost break-even threshold and three reproducible but low-confidence county comparison gaps. The county gaps use 2013-2020 pre-opening histories and an inverse-distance-weighted 20-county benchmark; very wide fit envelopes are retained because Santa Clara County matches poorly. No model converts capacity to consumption, permit value to jobs, or unidentified vendor and community activity to local benefits. prj_study_im3_building_01073720208: Second-pass governed synthesis for Google Council Bluffs. Construction job-years use only two directly observed September 2025 city permit valuations and transfer the published Prince William County prototype coefficients as benchmark equivalents; the four channels are separated and protected by one aggregation. No Pottawattamie County supplier-retention share is imposed because the public audit found contractor names but no payment or vendor-residence ledger. The water row is the unallocated Google Council Bluffs location identity reported for 2024, not a building allocation. No local abatement, exemption realization, franchise-fee amount, electric load, public-service cost, break-even threshold, or net fiscal result is modeled. County outcome gaps remain descriptive benchmark applications with fit-sensitivity ranges and no causal attribution. prj_study_im3_building_01132541700: Four bounded syntheses are retained after direct-record search: one deterministic conversion of Meta's rounded 2024 Henrico water-withdrawal observation and three governed, descriptive county comparison gaps. No construction, operating, supplier, household, tax-receipt, incentive-cost, or public-service-cost model is added because the public record lacks the needed project-specific bases and arbitrary allocation shares would create false precision. Every retained estimate is visibly modeled, unallocated to the selected building, non-additive, and noncausal. prj_study_im3_campus_00231769626: Residual synthesis after the Google The Dalles public-source audit. Only three low-confidence descriptive county comparison gaps are retained because the direct record does not identify causal county outcomes. Each benchmark uses the available 2001-2005 pre-opening history, excludes all study counties from a 20-county inverse-distance-weighted donor pool, and carries a fit-sensitivity envelope. No model converts broad investment or permit values to jobs, onsite contractor counts to supplier output, utility-system loads to campus consumption, tax bills to payments, or unmatched incentive formulas and public costs to a fiscal net.

project_description: State Farm Olathe is a single-tenant data center operated by State Farm Mutual Automobile Insurance Company at 24400 West Valley Parkway in Olathe, Johnson County, Kansas. City permit records document new construction in 2015 and a tenant finish in 2017, while SEC filings say the 193,953-square-foot facility was built in 2016, the lease began November 3, 2016, and State Farm occupied the property by early 2017. This account covers the single approximately 20-acre parcel and its building, not State Farm's wider portfolio, later unverified expansion, tenant equipment, or neighboring data centers.
